title: Agility: は and の as light, quick tools
summary: Japanese can make a topic (は) or box up a whole clause (の) with almost no effort, so sentences use them where English would feel heavy.

blocks.text: Languages differ in **agility**: how light and fast a tool is to use. A tool that is heavy in English may be nimble in Japanese, so Japanese uses it all the time. If you do not notice this, ordinary sentences feel odd.
は: a topic in one step

English "speaking of …" or "as for …" is clumsy, so you use it rarely. Japanese **は** is tiny, so it can be dropped in wherever you want to **set one thing against another**. The comment after a は topic is always a complete logical clause (lesson 60), and the new topic says: "what I say next may differ from what I said about the neighbor".

blocks.jp: この店はラーメンはおいしいが、カレーはまずい。
blocks.en: At this shop the ramen is good, but the curry is bad.

blocks.text: Here the clause carries two sub-topics. Each は contrasts: ramen against curry. Each one has its own hidden main carriage and engine.
ラーメンはおいしい。 As for ramen, (it) is good.
カレーはまずい。 As for curry, (it) is bad.
If the comment is the same, use **も** instead.
の: a whole clause in a noun box

The **nominalizing の** is a pronoun that bundles everything before it into a single noun, "the one that …". English needs preparation for "what she saw when she opened the door was …", but Japanese slips it in anywhere, even as a topic.
English needs preparation for "what she saw when she opened the door was ...": you have to build the sentence up in advance. Japanese slips the の in anywhere, even as a topic.

cars.label: the one that resounds in the morning town

blocks.text: 朝の町に響くのは鐘だ。 What resounds in the morning town is a bell.
So 朝の町に響くのは鐘だ is not "a bell resounds". It is an A-is-B sentence: A is "the one that resounds in the morning town" (topic), B is "a bell".

blocks.jp: 彼女が部屋で見たのは、古い人形だった。
blocks.en: What she saw in the room was an old doll.

blocks.jp: 毎朝歩くのは気持ちがいい。

items: **Agility** = how light a tool is. は and の are very light in Japanese.
**は** can be used again and again to set topics against each other; **も** says the comment is the same.
**の** turns a clause into a noun, "the one that …".
In a sentence like Xのは Y だ, X is the topic and Y is the answer.

questions.instruction: Which particle sets one thing against another?
questions.note: は is so light that you can use it again and again to contrast topics.

questions.instruction: If the comment is the same for a second thing, which particle do you use?
questions.note: も says "also": the same comment applies.

questions.instruction: What do the two は do?
questions.prompt: この店は魚はおいしいが、肉はまずい。
questions.note: Each は sets its topic against the other.
questions.en: At this shop the fish is good, but the meat is bad.

questions.instruction: Fill the gap
questions.prompt: 彼が書いた＿＿は手紙だった。
questions.note: の bundles the clause into a noun: the one that he wrote.
questions.en: What he wrote was a letter.

questions.instruction: Fill the gap
questions.prompt: 朝、走る＿＿は気持ちがいい。
questions.note: の turns 朝、走る into a noun so it can be the topic.
questions.en: Running in the morning feels good.

questions.instruction: What is the topic of this sentence?
questions.prompt: 駅にいたのは弟だった。
options: 駅にいたの (the one who was at the station)
questions.note: のは makes a whole clause the topic; 弟 is the answer.
questions.en: The one who was at the station was my younger brother.

questions.instruction: What kind of sentence is Xのは Yだ?
options: An A-is-B sentence: X is the topic, Y the answer
questions.note: X (the one that …) is B's topic and Y is the answer.

questions.instruction: What is the nominalizing の?
options: A pronoun that bundles a clause into a noun
questions.note: It means "the one that …".

questions.instruction: True or false?
questions.prompt: 私が食べたのは魚だ。 魚 is the answer in an A-is-B sentence.
questions.note: A = the one I ate; B = fish.

questions.instruction: What does "agility" mean in this lesson?
options: How light and quick a tool is to use
questions.note: は and の are nimble in Japanese, so they are used all the time.

questions.instruction: What follows a は topic?
options: A complete clause: 毎朝走っている
questions.note: The comment after は is a complete logical clause.
questions.en: My younger brother runs every morning.

questions.instruction: Which English phrase is closest to は?
questions.note: English needs a clumsy phrase; Japanese just uses は.

questions.instruction: What are the two は contrasting?
questions.prompt: 朝は雨だったが、午後は天気がよかった。
questions.note: Each topic is set against the other: morning versus afternoon.
questions.en: It was raining in the morning, but the weather was good in the afternoon.

questions.instruction: Which sentence is an A-is-B sentence with a bundled clause as the topic?
questions.note: 走ったの is the topic and 弟 is the answer.

questions.instruction: Tap the nominalizing の
questions.note: の bundles 駅にいた into a noun: the one who was at the station.
questions.en: The one who was at the station was my younger brother.

questions.instruction: Tap the topic (the clause that became a noun)
questions.note: 毎日走るの = the thing of running every day.

questions.instruction: Tap the answer (B) of this A-is-B sentence
questions.note: A is what I saw; B is an old photo.
questions.en: What I saw was an old photo.

questions.instruction: Build the sentence
questions.prompt: What I learned at school was hiragana.
questions.note: 学校で習ったの is the topic; ひらがなだ is the answer.
questions.en: What I learned at school was hiragana.

questions.instruction: Build the sentence
questions.prompt: I eat meat but not fish.
questions.note: Each は sets one food against the other.
questions.en: I eat meat but not fish.

questions.instruction: Build the sentence
questions.note: 旅行するの is the nominalized topic.

questions.instruction: Build the sentence
questions.prompt: What I saw yesterday was an interesting movie.
questions.note: 昨日見たの is the topic; the answer comes last.
questions.en: What I saw yesterday was an interesting movie.

questions.instruction: Which sentence sets two things against each other?
options: 魚は食べるが、肉は食べない。
questions.note: Two は set one thing against another.

questions.instruction: Tap the answer (B) of this A-is-B sentence
questions.note: Xのは Y だ: Y is the answer.
questions.en: What I bought yesterday is this book.
